policies.description: Any request to create or update a record must validate that all required (mandatory) fields are provided and non‑empty before invoking the tool.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: If a mandatory field required by the tool is missing, the assistant must not ask for further information but must state which field is required and halt the operation.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: The assistant must never assume, fabricate, or guess identifiers (such as location_id) before the API call; it must rely solely on the verified response from the add_location tool.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.description: Only one validated operation (add_location) may be performed at a time; the assistant must ensure all pre‑conditions are satisfied before invoking the tool.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: If a user request violates any rule in the policy document, the assistant must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: When an API call returns an error, the assistant must handle it according to the defined error handling policy: return a 403 Forbidden for permission issues, a 409 Conflict for record locking or state conflicts, and apply exponential backoff on rate‑limit violations.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).
409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.
Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.description: The assistant must not ask the user for confirmation or permission before invoking the add_location tool; it should proceed directly after validating the request.
references: You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.

policies.description: All actions must be performed in a logical and efficient order, ensuring that prerequisite checks (e.g., mandatory field validation) are completed before calling the add_location tool.
references: • Complete each task in a logical, and efficient execution flow.

policies.description: If a required identifier (such as a location name that already exists) is missing from the request, the assistant must perform a lookup using the appropriate tool, verify the correct value from prior responses, and use that retrieved data rather than fabricating an identifier.
references: • When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.description: A user may create a new location only if they have the Administrator role, which has full CRUD access across all tables. Users with Manager, Agent, or Reporter roles do not have create permission on the location table.
references: | Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

| Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations. |
